faq: Do I need a funnel in place already?
No. If you only have a website and a contact form, that is your funnel, and we map it. If you have nothing yet, we design the simplest path that fits your offer.
Will you change my site while mapping?
No. Mapping is a review and a plan. Building the pages, forms and follow-ups is done through our other lead generation services, which you can order after you see the plan.
What do you need from me?
Links to your site, forms and any landing pages, plus view access to your analytics if you have it. A short note on who your best customers are helps us judge the path.
Does the plan include traffic sources?
It shows how people arrive today and where new traffic could enter. Running paid ads or SEO is separate, but the plan tells you which source suits each step.
desc:
Lead generation funnel mapping draws the path a stranger takes from first visit to first conversation, then shows where people drop out. Ecom Swift LLC walks your real pages, forms and follow-ups and gives you a clear diagram with a ranked list of fixes.

## What is lead generation funnel mapping?

Lead generation funnel mapping is a written and drawn review of every step between a stranger finding you and a person starting a conversation. The steps usually include a source such as search or social media, a landing page, a form or booking, a confirmation and a follow-up message. The map shows how those parts connect and where the chain is weak.

It is a plan, not a rebuild. Nothing is changed in your accounts while we map, so there is no risk to what already works.

## Why a funnel needs a map

Most small businesses grow their lead path one piece at a time. A form here, a page there, an email tool added later. After a while no one can say what a visitor actually experiences from start to finish. Broken links, forms that go to the wrong inbox and follow-ups that never send can sit unnoticed for months.

A map makes the whole path visible at once. You can see which steps exist, which are missing and which are doing nothing useful. That clarity stops you from spending money on traffic that leads into a weak path.

## How mapping improves your results

When you know where visitors leave, you can fix the step that matters most rather than guessing. A single confusing form or a missing confirmation page may hold back more leads than a dozen small design tweaks. Ranking fixes by effort lets you start with the quick wins and plan bigger changes properly.

The map also helps you judge new ideas. Before adding another page or tool, you can check where it would sit in the path and what it would change. Mapping does not promise more leads on its own, and outcomes depend on your offer and traffic, but it points your effort at the right place.

## What a great funnel map includes

- A diagram that reads from first visit to first conversation on one page.
- Each entry point, such as search, ads, social media, email and referrals.
- Every page, form, booking and message a visitor meets along the way.
- A walkthrough of the path on both a phone and a computer.
- Marked gaps, such as missing thank-you pages or follow-ups.
- Notes on confusing wording, slow pages and extra steps.
- A ranked fix list showing the effort for each change.
- A better target path drawn beside the current one.
- Simple measures to watch at each step.
- A short written summary in plain words.

## What we do

We ask you to describe how leads reach you today and which tools you use. Then we walk the path ourselves as a first-time visitor, from each main entry point, noting what we see, click and receive. We record the pages, forms, emails and texts involved and draw them as one connected diagram.

We then mark the gaps and rank the fixes. Higher packages map more than one funnel, show where visitors enter by source, draw a stronger target funnel and add briefs for each missing page or form. The largest package includes an outline of follow-up messages, a suggested order for building the changes and a walkthrough call to talk through the plan. If you want us to build the fixes afterward, we can do that as separate work.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Map the funnel that matters most to your income first.
- Test every step on a phone, not only on a computer.
- Note where leads actually come from, not where you hope they come from.
- Fix the biggest gap before polishing small details.
- Keep the map and update it when you change a page.

**Avoid:**
- Adding new tools before you understand the existing path.
- Treating a missing follow-up as a minor detail.
- Judging the funnel only from your own account while logged in.
- Trying to repair every issue in a single week.
- Mapping an ideal funnel that ignores your real pages.

## Who this service is for

This service suits an owner who gets some leads but cannot explain why they come or why others vanish. It also helps a business about to spend on ads that wants to check the path first. A new offer with no funnel yet is another fit, since the map becomes a build plan.

## What we need from you

Send the links to your main pages, forms and booking tools, and a short note on who you want to reach. If you already send follow-up emails, share a sample. We do not need passwords, and during mapping we usually need no access at all. If a deeper check helps, you can give view access as a collaborator or staff user.
